facts.statement: Qianxisaurus is classified as an extinct genus of pachypleurosaur or alternatively as a basal eosauropterygian.
facts.quote: Qianxisaurus is an extinct genus of pachypleurosaur or alternatively a basal eosauropterygian

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Middle Triassic (Ladinian age) in Guizhou Province, southwestern China.
facts.quote: known from the Middle Triassic (Ladinian age) of Guizhou Province, southwestern China

facts.statement: The species is known only from a single nearly complete and articulated holotype skeleton.
facts.quote: Qianxisaurus is known solely from the holotype NMNS-KIKO-F044630, a nearly complete and articulated skeleton

facts.statement: The skull of the holotype specimen measures 7.6 cm in length.
facts.quote: The skull measures at 7.6 cm in length

facts.statement: The total estimated body length of the individual is over 80 cm.
facts.quote: the total length of the individual is estimated to have been over 80 cm

facts.statement: The holotype was discovered in 2006 near the Huangnihe River at Chajiang in southwestern Guizhou Province.
facts.quote: NMNS-KIKO-F044630 was discovered in 2006 near the Huangnihe River at Chajiang of Xingyi, southwesternmost Guizhou Province

facts.statement: The fossils date to the Ladinian stage of the late Middle Triassic, approximately 238 million years ago.
facts.quote: thus dating to the Ladinian stage of the late Middle Triassic, about 238 million years ago

facts.statement: The specimen was most likely collected from the Zhuganpo Member of the Falang Formation.
facts.quote: It was most probably collected from the Zhuganpo Member of the Falang Formation

facts.statement: The genus was first described and named by Yen-Nien Cheng, Xiao-Chun Wu, Tamaki Sato, and Hsi-Yin Shan in 2012.
facts.quote: Qianxisaurus was first described and named by Yen-Nien Cheng, Xiao-Chun Wu, Tamaki Sato and Hsi-Yin Shan in 2012

facts.statement: The generic name includes the Greek word saûros, meaning 'lizard'.
facts.quote: and from Greek saûros (σαῦρος), Latinized as saurus, meaning "lizard"

facts.statement: The specific name is derived from Chajiang, the town near which the specimen was collected.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from Chajiang, a town near which the specimen was collected

facts.statement: The animal possesses a premaxilla with eight teeth.
facts.quote: Qianxisaurus bears a premaxilla with eight teeth

facts.statement: Qianxisaurus shares a longitudinal groove on the upper-back-facing surface of its dorsal ribs exclusively with the basal pistosauroids Corosaurus, Sanchiaosaurus, Kwangsisaurus, and Chinchenia.
facts.quote: Qianxisaurus shares the presence of a longitudinal groove on upper-back-facing surface of dorsal ribs exclusively with the potential basal pistosauroids Corosaurus, Sanchiaosaurus, Kwangsisaurus and Chinchenia

facts.statement: The time range for the genus is the Ladinian, from 241.464 to 237 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ladinian to Ladinian (241.464 to 237 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The generic name is derived from Qianxi, referring to the western part of Guizhou Province where the holotype was found.
rejected.quote: The generic name is derived from Qianxi, which refers to the western part of Guizhou Province where the holotype was found
